suggestedBy: Claude (AI). Alternatives with the same function, chosen from generic Ökobaudat data.
note: A swap keeps the layer thickness and volume share. Structural and thermal equivalence must be checked separately.

Masonry - Concrete Block.reason: Lightweight block from natural pumice. Far less cement per m³ (500 kg/m³). Check the load-bearing capacity: the blocks are lighter and weaker.
Expanded-clay concrete block for outer walls, 501 kg/m³. A common lightweight masonry unit in Germany.

Masonry - Brick.reason: Sand-lime facing brick instead of fired clay. No kiln firing, so roughly half the A1–A3 per m³. It looks different (light grey or white).

Insulation / Thermal Barriers - Rigid in.reason: Mineral wool facade board. About a third of the carbon of XPS. λ is similar (≈0.035), so the U-value hardly changes.
Wood fibre board. Stores biogenic carbon, so A1–A3 is negative. λ ≈ 0.040 is worse than XPS, so it needs about 15% more thickness for the same U-value (the swap keeps the thickness).
EPS instead of XPS. Lower density, so less carbon per m³ at a similar λ.

Concrete - Cast In Situ.reason: Ready-mix C25/30 with recycled aggregate. Same strength class, a small saving.

Ceramic Tile.reason: Unglazed stoneware tile. Leaving out the glaze firing cuts A1–A3 by about 60%.

Plasterboard.reason: Clay panel instead of gypsum board, for interior linings. Similar carbon, but no gypsum to landfill at end of life.

Wood - Flooring.reason: Multi-layer parquet. A thinner hardwood wear layer on a softwood core, so less timber per m².
